mission.display_title: Use the credibility premium formula and factor

mission.learning_objective: Explain the credibility premium formula and the role played by the credibility factor.
mission.concept_focus: Premium = Z·X̄ + (1−Z)·μ → role of Z → refuse Z=1 myth.

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 5.1.6
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Write the credibility premium as a blend of observed mean and prior/manual mean using credibility factor Z. What does Z near 1 mean?
hints: Use CMP language from today's notes.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: P = Z·X̄ + (1−Z)·μ. Z near 1 → heavy weight on data; near 0 → heavy weight on prior/manual mean.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Skipping the LO hinge or swallowing the next LO.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 5.1.6
knowledge_checks.prompt: Refuse: 'always use full credibility (Z=1).' When might Z be smaller?
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Refuse Z=1 always. With limited/noisy data, Z shrinks toward the prior/manual mean.
